subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: Should experimental Claws removal remain a core lifecycle feature that can orchestrate config, workspace, session, and package cleanup under one consent-bound plan, or should its scope stop at releasing provenance until a broader lifecycle owner is accepted?
rationale: The branch is technically structured around a product-level ownership policy: which resources core may remove, when referenced resources can be escalated to uninstall, and whether this orchestration belongs in the experimental core CLI rather than a narrower owner surface.

options.title: Sponsor the lifecycle contract
options.body: Accept the plan-first core removal boundary, contingent on exact-head proof of the referenced cleanup conflict and override paths.

options.title: Narrow removal to release-only
options.body: Retain agent and provenance removal while leaving referenced package cleanup to explicit canonical package commands until the ownership policy is finalized.

options.title: Pause the stacked slice
options.body: Defer this PR until the RFC and parent package-lifecycle contract have an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Accept the plan-first core removal boundary, contingent on exact-head proof of the referenced cleanup conflict and override paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Their RFC review directly articulated the package-removal ownership requirement that determines this PR's boundary.
